reason: Layer 2 names point at the base-16 tokens (--black: var(--color-0), and so on), so one edit to --color-N re-themes the names, the framework tokens and --mix. P writes each colour out as a literal. The resolved colours are the same values; the theme creator and --mix both read --color-N.

New tint tokens. The dark block carries a literal default for each tint, as :root does, so a browser without color-mix() keeps a readable pale fill in dark mode. The color-mix() versions replace these under @supports.

New tint tokens. The @supports block that holds the color-mix() versions targets :root and [data-theme], so a nested data-theme container recomputes its own tints from its own --background. The :root half passes as an extra custom property; this is the other half of the same rule.
